title: Prompt Injection and Trust Boundaries
summary: A model cannot reliably tell instructions from data, so text from an attacker can steer it. This lesson quantifies attack success, separates direct from indirect injection, and builds defence in depth around trust boundaries, least privilege and layered checks, because no prompt-only defence is complete.
objectives: Explain why prompt injection exists in terms of the single token sequence a model reads
Measure attack success rate with a confidence interval and compute the chance an attacker succeeds in N attempts
Distinguish direct from indirect injection and estimate exposure from the rate of poisoned content
Draw trust boundaries and apply least privilege so that a successful injection has bounded impact
Combine layered defences and reason about residual risk, including correlation between layers
Tune a guardrail classifier threshold when attacks are rare, using precision, recall and costs
prerequisites: You should know how a prompt is rendered into one token sequence and about the instruction hierarchy ([Anatomy of a Prompt](/learn/prompt-and-context/prompt-anatomy)), tool calling ([Tool Definitions and Function Calling](/learn/prompt-and-context/tools-and-functions)), and basic probability of independent events. Precision and recall are explained as they appear.
